docs.title: Trace a game session
docs.text:
1. Give both Unity clients the same pseudonymous player ID.
  2. When Summit returns a session UUID, attach it to the Trailhead recording.
  3. Send analytics to Summit and replay data to Trailhead during or after play, according to the recording client in the game.
  4. Open the session in Summit and follow the Trailhead link after the summary sync. The replay's recording ID is separate from the Summit session UUID.

Connect Summit and Trailhead in Unity or try the SludgeTower verification walkthrough. For experience-specific material, see the existing Unity XR user documentation and the Horticulture developer docs.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide will walk you through setting up your local development environment for the LXD extension. Follow the steps below to create your local branches, install dependencies, build local changes, and test your work.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Git: Ensure you have Git installed and configured.
  • Node.js & npm: Verify that your Node.js and npm installations are up-to-date.
  • Existing Tools:
  • lxd-tools repository
  • GitHub Desktop(optional): Depending on your familiarity working with Git in the command line, GitHub Desktop may be a helpful tool for pulling repos and committing your code changes.

docs.title: 1. Create a Local Branch of lxd-tools
docs.text:
1. Clone the lxd-tools repository:

git clone <URL_TO_LXD_TOOLS_REPOSITORY>

cd lxd-tools

  1. Install dependencies:

npm install

Note: These dependencies are also defined in the package.json of lxd-tools.

docs.title: 2. Starting Development
docs.text:
1. At this point, you should test if you're able to build the extension locally. In the lxd-tools directory, run npm run build. If that fails, you will need to address any errors.

  2. If your build is successful, you are ready to start working on code. Work can be done either in the current release branch(for small changes), your own testing branch, or a feature branch(if the work you're doing will go on to be it's own feature.) Make sure you checkout/create a branch that isn't main before you begin working.

  3. After you made changes, please document them in the Unreleased section of the change log

docs.title: 3. Testing Your Changes
docs.text:
1. Once the local build is working and you're in a non-main branch, you can make changes to the code and test them in the browser. To have a build of the extension that updates every time the code is changed, you can run npm run watch.

  2. Jest is the testing suite used for unit testing. Any time you change code, you should run the tests to make sure they still pass. Tests can be run with the command npm test.

docs.title: 4. Finalizing Your Changes
docs.text:
• Features that have passed testing and are ready to go into the extension can be pushed to the current release branch.
  • Features that still need work may be best placed in their own feature branch.

docs.title: Publishing the Extension
docs.text: This guide explains how to publish the LXD Extension.

docs.title: 1. Prepare Your Branches
docs.text:
• Merge Changes Down: Ensure that finished code in feature or development branches are merged down into the release branch.
  • Push Commits: Before starting the publishing process, verify that all users' finished changes on the release branch have been pushed to the remote repository.

docs.title: 2. Update the Version Number
docs.text:
• Increment the Version in package.json:

  • Open package.json and update the version field to the next release version (e.g., from 2.9.1.2 to 2.9.1.3).

  • Versioning in incremented based on the following:

    +0.0.0.1 for a hotfix +0.0.1 for sprint-based releases +0.1 for feature releases +1.0 for massive changes

docs.title: 3. Run Tests
docs.text:
• Test the Code: Run the test suite to validate that all tests pass successfully: npm test

  • Fix Any Failures: If any tests fail, resolve the issues before proceeding.

docs.title: 4. Build Locally and Test Manually
docs.text:
• Build the extension locally for testing

Run npm run build to build the extension locally

  • Test the Local Build Version: Perform a manual test of the extension in its intended environment. Verify that all functionalities work as expected.

docs.title: 5. Publish the Extension
docs.text:
• Execute the Publishing Command: Once you've built the extension, publish the extension by running the publish script: npm run publish

The publish script performs the following tasks:

  • Checks the current version from package.json and creates the corresponding package tag.
  • Ensures that the tag does not already exist in the distribution folder’s Git history.
  • Updates Git tags.
  • Reads the manifest (manifest.source.json) and synchronizes its version with the package version.
  • Stages changes, constructs a commit message from the differences between tags, commits the changes, and finally pushes commit and tags to the remote repository.

docs.title: 6. Communicate & Finalize the Release
docs.text:
• Notify the Team: Let everyone know about the new release. The people that use the extension are in The Mighty LXD Team chat on Microsoft Teams. Let them know there's a new version of the extension, including a few top level details about what is new.

  • Merge Current Release Branch into main in LXD-Tools Merge the current release branch into main in the lxd-tools repository.

  • New Release Branch in LXD-Tools: Create a new release branch in lxd-tools based on the newly merged main branch.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
1. Merge Changes Down:
  2. Consolidate updates from various branches into the release branch.
  3. Increment the Version:
  4. Update the version number in package.json.
  5. Run Tests:
  6. Run npm test Ensure all tests pass (fix any failing tests).
  7. Build Locally
  8. Run npm run build to build the extension locally for testing.
  9. Manual Testing:
  10. Manually verify that the extension works as intended.
  11. Build & Publish:
  12. Run npm run publish to publish the extension.
  13. Notify the Team:
  14. Communicate the new release to the team.
  15. Manage Release Branches:
  16. Merge changes in lxd-tools to main.
  17. Create a new release branch in lxd-tools for the new version.

docs.title: Repository and architecture
docs.text:
This is a Manifest V3 browser extension for Unity Environmental University's Learning Experience Designers using Canvas. It targets Chrome-family browsers and Firefox. It is not a standalone web app: most UI runs inside authenticated Canvas pages, with separate extension popup and search pages.

  • webpack.config.js defines the entry points and generated manifests. manifest.source.json defines content-script routes, permissions, and browser identities. Keep these in sync when adding an entry point.
  • src/background/ handles extension messages and privileged browser operations. src/content/ contains injected page helpers and course navigation.
  • src/popup/ and src/search/ are extension pages; search integrates with LISA.
  • src/ui/ contains Canvas page integrations, including syllabus import, course navigation, modules, and SpeedGrader tools.
  • src/publish/ handles Blueprint publishing, migrations, profile content, and course validations/fixes. Validation contracts and registration live under src/publish/fixesAndUpdates/validations/; follow the active registry rather than assuming every validation file is enabled.
  • src/reporting/ and src/admin/ contain reporting and administrative UI.
  • src/canvas-redux/ contains shared Redux slices. Other features use their own state; follow the affected feature's existing pattern.
  • @ueu/ueu-canvas supplies Canvas API models and request utilities. It is an npm dependency, not source maintained in this repository. Check its installed declarations before assuming an export exists. src/canvasInstances.ts defines configurable Canvas origins/accounts.

docs.title: Setup and builds
docs.text:
Use npm and the committed package-lock.json; CI uses Node.js 24. Run npm ci after switching to a branch with different dependencies. Do not change source to work around an outdated node_modules installation.

Command Behavior npm run build Production build, minification and TypeScript checking; writes to sibling dist/. npm run build:dev Development build in sibling lxd-extension-build/, with a separate local extension identity. npm run watch Development watcher writing to dist/; retains the normal extension identity. npm run watch:dev Development watcher using the separate local build and identity.

Output paths resolve against the repository directory, not the shell working directory. The sibling layout supports a separate build repository and the CI workspace layout. BUILD_OUTPUT_DIR can override the output path, but the separate local identity is selected only for the exact lxd-extension-build/ override used by the dev scripts. Development builds transpile without type checking; run npm run typecheck separately. Generated artifacts are ignored; edit sources, not bundles. Version values in the generated manifest and update manifests come from package.json.

Load the relevant output folder as an unpacked extension. After rebuilding, reload that extension in the browser's extension manager and refresh existing Canvas tabs. If the browser shows an old version, check the loaded folder and its manifest.json; a successful build does not reload installed extensions. The default build does not update an in-repo dist/ folder. Check for duplicate installations before changing the output path. Multiple source checkouts under one parent directory share the same default output, so use isolated parent directories or an explicit BUILD_OUTPUT_DIR when testing worktrees.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• npm test -- --runInBand runs Jest once with a single worker. For focused checks, use npm test -- --runInBand --runTestsByPath <test-file>.
  • npm run typecheck runs TypeScript without emitting files.
  • npm run lint runs the flat ESLint configuration in eslint.config.mjs.
  • npm run build verifies the production bundles and manifest transforms.

CI runs tests, lint, and type checking on pushes; the PR build workflow also builds and uploads an unsigned extension. Run checks appropriate to code changes and report actual failures, including existing failures, rather than claiming a successful build proves tests pass. Documentation-only changes need link/path review, not new implementation tests.

Jest uses jsdom, ts-jest, aliases from tsconfig.json, shared fixtures under src/__mocks__/, and a browser API mock in src/__mocks__/runtime.ts. Tests generally sit beside the feature or in its __tests__/ directory. For DOM or extension lifecycle changes, also verify the relevant browser flow on a designated test course. Do not run course mutations against production courses just to validate a change.

docs.title: Implementation conventions
docs.text:
TypeScript is strict; reuse the existing @/ and @publish/ aliases and nearby React/Bootstrap patterns. Prefer existing Canvas models and request helpers, including src/fetch/apiWriteConfig.ts, over duplicating API plumbing. Canvas requests use the browser's authenticated session and CSRF handling, not a new standalone API key. Preserve the selected Canvas instance when constructing links and requests.

Parse fetched Canvas HTML with parseHtmlInert from src/utils/html.ts when inspecting or transforming it. Inert parsing is not sanitization for rendering untrusted HTML. Validate URL origins/hostnames structurally rather than checking whether a raw URL contains a trusted hostname. Keep browser message handlers, content scripts, and service-worker contexts distinct.

docs.title: Changes and releases
docs.text:
Work on a feature/fix branch, preferably in a separate worktree when the main checkout needs to stay unchanged. Preserve unrelated user files and changes. Document user-facing changes under Unreleased in CHANGELOG.md.

Use .github/workflows/ as the authority for current automation:

  • push-test.yaml: tests, lint, and types on pushes.
  • build-testing.yml: PR/manual unsigned builds; artifacts come from dist at the workspace root because Actions checks out the source into lxd-tools/ and webpack writes to its sibling dist/.
  • main-deploy.yml: production signing, R2 uploads/pruning, build-repository sync, tags, and release branches on eligible pushes/manual runs from main.
  • version-check.yml: requires a changed package version for applicable PRs into main; Markdown/YAML-only and release-tools-only changes are excluded.

Keep build, packaging, artifact discovery, and distribution-copy paths aligned when changing output locations. Release tools have their own lockfile under .github/release-tools/. See docs/BUILD_PROCESS.md for deployment details and docs/SYLLABUS_SYNC.md for syllabus behavior. Some README publishing instructions describe the older manual process; verify them against the workflows.

Signing, publishing, deployment dispatch, and merging are separate actions from building or opening a PR. Keep private signing keys, tokens, .env files, and browser/session data out of commits and artifacts.

docs.title: LXD Chrome Extension
docs.text:
This extension is for use by Unity Environmental University Learning Experience Designers working in Canvas.

Source repository: https://github.com/Unity-Environmental-University/lxd-tools

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
For most people who use this extension at Unity, it should now automatically install on your laptop. If it doesn't, you can follow the steps below:

  1. Clone this repository
  2. If you have GitHub Desktop installed, select Code → Open with GitHub Desktop
  3. Otherwise, select Code → Download ZIP, then extract the zip and place the folder somewhere easy to find
  4. Load the extension into Chrome:
  5. Go to chrome://extensions
  6. Enable Developer Mode (toggle in the top-right corner)
  7. Click Load unpacked and select the folder where you placed the extension files

Full walkthrough: https://webkul.com/blog/how-to-install-the-unpacked-extension-in-chrome/

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
1. If you are using GitHub Desktop, pull the latest version of this repository
  2. If you downloaded a ZIP:
  3. Download a fresh ZIP and extract it
  4. Replace all files in your original installation folder with the new ones, keeping the same filenames
  5. Go to chrome://extensions and click the Update button at the top of the page

GitHub Desktop download: https://desktop.github.com/

docs.title: Extension Popup
docs.text:
Click the extension icon in your browser toolbar (or press Alt+Shift+F) to open the popup panel. From here you can:

  • Search for courses by course code and jump directly to them in Canvas
  • Filter by subaccount (Distance Education, Distance Education Development, Unity College)
  • Open Salesforce reports with one click:
  • Undergrad Section Check
  • Grad Section Check
  • Unique Course Offerings by Term
  • Save your OpenAI API key (used by AI-powered features in the extension — see Advanced Options)

docs.title: Course Navigation Buttons
docs.text:
When viewing any Canvas course, the extension adds buttons to the top of the page:

Button What it does DEV Opens the DEV_ version of this course in a new tab BP Opens the Blueprint version of this course in a new tab BPs Shows a list of all available Blueprint versions of this course SECTIONS Opens all student sections linked to this Blueprint

These buttons try to take you to the same page you are currently on (e.g., the same assignment or discussion) in the corresponding course version. If a matching page is not found, the course home page opens instead.

docs.title: Quick Course Search (Keyboard Shortcut)
docs.text:
Press Alt+Shift+F to open a quick-search dialog. You can type:

Query Result DEV_TEST000 Navigate directly to that course w2a Open all assignments in Week 2 w2q Open all quizzes in Week 2 w2d Open all discussions in Week 2 w3d2 Go to the second discussion in Week 3 w1d0 Go to the course Introduction (usually Week 1, Discussion 0) DEV_TEST000\|w3q1 Go to the first quiz in Week 3 of a different course

docs.title: Links Button
docs.text: On any Canvas content page (pages, assignments, discussions), a Links button appears in the header. Clicking it opens all external links and file links embedded in that page in new tabs at once — useful for quickly checking that all resources in a lesson are accessible.

docs.title: Modules Page
docs.text:
When viewing the Modules page of a course, the extension adds two buttons to the header:

  • Lock All (Blueprint courses only) — Locks every module item in the Blueprint with a single click. The page reloads automatically when done.
  • Adjust Due Dates — Prompts you for a number of days, then shifts all assignment due dates in the course by that amount. Useful when copying a course to a new term.

docs.title: Rubric Reordering
docs.text:
When editing a rubric, the extension adds reordering controls to each rubric criterion row:

  • ↑ / ↓ buttons to move a criterion up or down
  • Drag and drop rows to reorder them directly (the dragged row turns semi-transparent, and a blue border shows the drop target)

The reorder controls appear when you enter edit mode and disappear when you save or cancel.

docs.title: SpeedGrader — Rubric Score Exports
docs.text:
On the Canvas SpeedGrader page, the extension adds export buttons to the gradebook header:

Button What it exports Rubrics: Assignment Rubric scores for the current assignment → Rubric Scores {AssignmentName}.csv Rubrics: Section Rubric scores for all assignments in the course → Rubric Scores {CourseCode}.csv ... (three dots) Opens a date-range picker to export scores for a specific term window → {CourseCode}-{StartDate}-{EndDate}.csv

A loading indicator appears while the export is being generated.

docs.title: Syllabus — Import Week 1 Materials
docs.text:
On the Course Syllabus page, an Import Wk1 Mats button appears above the "Week 1 Learning Materials" section. Clicking it:

  1. Reads the course's "Week 1 Learning Materials" page
  2. Extracts all video embeds and learning material boxes from that page
  3. Replaces the existing syllabus content in that section with the imported materials
  4. Resizes embedded video iframes to fit the syllabus layout

The page reloads automatically after a successful import.

docs.title: Large Image Warning
docs.text: When editing a Canvas page that contains a banner image wider than 2000px, the extension displays a prominent warning around the image. A Try Resize button appears — clicking it attempts to resize the image to 1200px wide.

docs.title: Home Tile Image Generator
docs.text:
On a course's Module Home section, a Generate Home Tiles button appears. This tool automatically creates marketing thumbnail images for the course:

  • Use Course Image checkbox — uses the course's banner image as the source (checked by default)
  • Module Number field — specify a module number as the image source (use 0 for the course-level image)
  • Click Generate to produce two image files:
  • {CourseCode}DetailImage.png (1920px wide)
  • {CourseCode}ListImage.png (600px wide)
  • A Salesforce Image Download button is also available to extract and download course images in Salesforce-compatible formats

docs.title: Version Update Notice

If a newer version of the extension is available, a banner appears on Canvas course pages alerting you:

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This document describes the automated build and deployment process for the LXD browser extension. The workflow runs when a change is pushed to the main branch (in practice, when a pull request is merged) or when it is started manually from main, and handles building, signing, and distributing the extension across multiple platforms (Chrome and Firefox).

The deployment pipeline manages version control, package signing, storage on Cloudflare R2, and maintains a clean version history.

docs.title: When the workflow runs
docs.text:
• A push to the main branch, which in practice means a pull request was merged (branch protection requires a pull request for main)
  • If the push only changes .md, .yml, .yaml and/or .github/release-tools/ files, the workflow will not run. This allows documentation and workflows to be iterated separately of release cycles.
  • A manual run (Actions → "Deploy Extension Updates" → Run workflow). This is a fallback, for example to re-run a deploy that failed partway. It always builds the tip of main.

docs.title: What triggers it NOT to run
docs.text:
• Pull request is closed without merging, opened or updated
  • A manual run started on any ref other than main (the job is skipped)

Test builds that must not publish use the separate Build testing workflow (build-testing.yml), which runs on pull requests and can be started manually for any branch. It uploads an unsigned dist/ as a workflow artifact and never uses the secrets below.

docs.title: Repository requirements
docs.text:
• Version number in package.json is updated with each release
  • Extension source code follows the npm build pipeline
  • updates.json and update.xml files are present in the dist directory

docs.title: Secrets and credentials
docs.text:
These are stored as secrets of the production GitHub environment, whose deployment branches are limited to main. Only the deploy job (environment: production) can read them, so workflows on other branches cannot.

Secret Name Purpose CHROME_KEY_PEM_B64 Base64-encoded Chrome extension signing key (PEM format) WEB_EXT_API_KEY Firefox AMO API key for signing WEB_EXT_API_SECRET Firefox AMO API secret for signing R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID Cloudflare R2 access key ID for storage R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Cloudflare R2 secret access key CF_ACCOUNT_ID Cloudflare account ID for R2 endpoint R2_BUCKET_NAME Name of the Cloudflare R2 bucket for storage LXD_TOOLS_BUILD_TOKEN GitHub personal access token for lxd-tools-build repository

docs.title: Build Process Steps
docs.text:
The workflow performs the following automated steps in sequence:

  1. Repository Checkout & Setup — Clones the lxd-tools repository, sets up Node.js 24 and installs dependencies from the lockfile with npm ci. The packaging tools (crx3, web-ext) are installed at pinned versions from .github/release-tools/ (see Updating the release tools). Git tags are fetched to enable version detection.
  2. Version Validation — Reads the version from package.json and verifies it hasn't been deployed before by checking for an existing git tag. If a duplicate version is detected, the entire build fails with a clear error message to prevent accidental re-deployment.
  3. Extension Compilation — Runs npm run build to compile the extension source code into the dist directory.
  4. Platform-Specific Signing — The compiled extension is signed for both platforms:
  5. Chrome: Uses the crx3 tool with the private key to produce lxd-extension-{VERSION}.crx

  6. Firefox: Uses the web-ext sign command with AMO API credentials to produce lxd-extension-{VERSION}.xpi signed for the unlisted channel

  7. Artifact Verification — Validates that all required output files exist: both signed extensions (.crx and .xpi), plus the update manifests (updates.json and update.xml). File paths are captured for downstream steps.

  8. Upload to Cloudflare R2 — All artifacts are uploaded to the R2 bucket with appropriate content types. This includes both signed extensions and update manifests needed by the browser extension update mechanisms.
  9. Version Pruning — Automatically deletes old versions from R2, keeping only the 5 most recent releases of each file type (.crx and .xpi). This reduces storage costs while maintaining version history.
  10. Sync to Build Repository — The entire dist directory is copied to the lxd-tools-build repository on the stable branch, creating an audit trail of all deployments with commits attributed to github-actions[bot].
  11. Git Release Management — A git tag matching the version number is created and pushed, and a corresponding release branch (release/{VERSION}) is created for long-term reference and potential rollback scenarios.

docs.title: Version Management
docs.text:
• package.json version must be incremented BEFORE merging the PR
  • The pull reqest will be blocked from merging unless the package version is bumped
  • Duplicate version deployments are prevented by version validation step
  • If version already exists, entire build fails with clear error message

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• The deploy job only runs from main and uses the production environment; the secrets are not available to other branches
  • All secrets are referenced via ${{ secrets.VAR_NAME }} syntax, per GitHub Actions format
  • Chrome key is base64-encoded; it is decoded to the runner's temp directory only inside the pack step and deleted when that step ends
  • Firefox API credentials are environment variables, never logged
  • GitHub token used for pushing to build repository is scoped and temporary

docs.title: Storage Retention
docs.text:
• Only the 5 most recent versions are retained in R2
  • Older versions are automatically pruned to control costs
  • This applies to both .xpi and .crx files

docs.title: Repository Structure
docs.text:
• Source code: lxd-tools repository (main branch)
  • Built artifacts: lxd-tools-build repository (stable branch)
  • This separation allows history tracking and rollback capability

docs.title: Workflow Execution Environment
docs.text:
• Runner: ubuntu-22.04
  • Permissions: contents: write (for creating tags and commits)
  • Duration: Typically 5-10 minutes depending on npm install time

docs.title: File Outputs
docs.text:
After successful execution, the following files are available:

File Location Platform Purpose lxd-extension-{VERSION}.crx R2 bucket & dist/ Chrome Signed extension package lxd-extension-{VERSION}.xpi R2 bucket & dist/ Firefox Signed extension package update.xml R2 bucket & dist/ Chrome Update manifest for Chrome updates.json R2 bucket & dist/ Firefox Update manifest for Firefox

docs.title: Build fails at version validation
docs.text:
Cause: package.json version was not incremented

Solution:

  1. Update package.json with a new version number
  2. Land the change on main through a new pull request that includes the bump

docs.title: Re-running a failed deploy
docs.text:
After fixing the cause, start the workflow manually from main (Actions → "Deploy Extension Updates" → Run workflow).

  • If the failed run had already pushed the version tag, delete the tag first (git push --delete origin {VERSION}), and also the release/{VERSION} branch if it was created. Otherwise the duplicate-version check stops the new run.
  • If the failure came after the Firefox signing step, AMO has already used that version number and will reject signing it again. Bump the version through a new pull request instead.

docs.title: Chrome extension fails to sign
docs.text:
Cause: Invalid or missing CHROME_KEY_PEM_B64 secret

Solution:

  1. Verify the secret is properly base64-encoded
  2. Check that the PEM file is valid (openssl x509 -in cert.pem -text -noout)
  3. Update the secret in GitHub repository settings if needed
  4. Re-run the workflow

docs.title: Monitoring and Notifications
docs.text:
The workflow produces the following artifacts for monitoring:

  • GitHub Actions logs: Real-time build output in Actions tab
  • Git tags: Version tags created on successful deployment (visible in Releases)
  • Release branches: Version-specific branches created at release/{VERSION}
  • lxd-tools-build commits: Automatic commits showing deployment history

docs.title: Before modifying the workflow
docs.text:
1. Test changes in a separate branch
  2. Ensure all secrets are still available
  3. Verify npm build script still works
  4. Test signing keys are still valid
  5. Review and test any version management changes

docs.title: Updating the release tools
docs.text: crx3 and web-ext are pinned in .github/release-tools/package.json and its own package-lock.json, separate from the extension's dependencies so the root overrides do not apply to them. To update them, change the versions there, run npm install in that folder, and commit both files. A pull request that only changes .github/release-tools/ does not start the deploy workflow and does not need a version bump; the new versions are used by the next release. The Build testing workflow runs npm ci --ignore-scripts in that folder on every pull request, so an out-of-sync lockfile fails the PR.

docs.title: Canvas Authentication
docs.text:
The extension does not use a standalone API Key. Instead, it piggybacks on the user’s active browser session. It authorizes requests by extracting the Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) token that Canvas already generated for the user.

Where we get it:

Primary: A hidden input field in the Canvas DOM: input[name='authenticity_token'].

Fallback: The browser cookie named \_csrf_token(which the extension manually decodes).

NOTE: If the university updates Canvas and they change the name of that input field or the cookie, all POST/PUT requests will fail (403 Forbidden).

docs.title: Link checking
docs.text:
Find a link in Canvas HTML

Parse the syllabus or discussion body with parseHtmlInert. Select anchors with a[href] and compare each anchor's getAttribute("href") with the expected value. An href that contains the URL inside a redirect has a different attribute value.

Check the current page's hostname

When checking whether the current page URL belongs to a trusted host, parse the URI with new URL() and check the hostname property: new URL(document.documentURI).hostname.endsWith(".instructure.com"). Never use .includes() on a raw URL string to check the host — a URL like https://evil.com/?r=https://unity.instructure.com would falsely pass. See content/index.ts.

docs.title: Syllabus Sync
docs.text:
Syllabus Sync brings a course's syllabus up to date with the current syllabus template while keeping everything that belongs to the course. Use it when updating a course to keep the syllabus current.

It is the Sync Syllabus button next to the Update Start Date button.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Using Sync

  1. Click Sync Syllabus in the Content Fixes window. A green "synced successfully" box appears and clears itself; a blue box stays.
  2. Open the syllabus (View syllabus) and look it over.
  3. If something is wrong, click Undo sync (in the blue box or at the top of the syllabus page). If it looks right, click Looks good.
  4. Sync replaces everything except the course specific information.
  5. Undo only works from the same browser, for the most recent sync, within 7 days. If a red error box appears instead, nothing was changed; see If an error message appears.

Editing the course information table (in the syllabus editor, at the top of the page)

  • Edit the table, not the syllabus text. The text on the page is filled in from the table, so anything typed over it is lost.
  • Don't rename, add, or delete rows. The left column names (course-title, textbook, and so on) are how values are found.
  • Lists are typed on one line with | between items. Outcomes become a numbered list (don't type the numbers); the textbook becomes a bulleted list when it has more than one item.
  • || and ||| make sub-bullets (textbook only): Lab kit | Supplies || Gloves || Goggles.
  • A | can't be part of an item's text; use a dash or comma.
  • Links, bold, and italics work in the textbook only. Links must start with http://, https://, or mailto:. Everything else shows as plain text.
  • Term and dates are updated by the Update Start Date tool, so they rarely need typing by hand.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Sync takes the template syllabus (undergraduate, graduate, or Career Edge) and rebuilds the syllabus from it. All course-specific information is retained:

Kept from the DEV course Where it lives The course information table (title, term, dates, credits, description, outcomes, textbook) A table at the top of the syllabus, see below The banner image The image at the top of the syllabus The Instructor Name: See Homepage line The first box, with the link to the course's own home page The Week 1 Learning Materials Preview box Its own box lower in the syllabus

Anything else in the syllabus outside those four places is replaced by the template's version.

docs.title: Before syncing
docs.text:
The syllabus must already have the course specific data table(only visible in edit mode) and have a Week 1 Learning Materials Preview box. If either is missing, sync can't tell which parts belong to the course and stops without changing anything.

Skim the syllabus once beforehand to know what to compare against afterward.

docs.title: What to expect
docs.text:
1. Click Sync Syllabus.
  2. After a moment, a green box at the top of the window says "Syllabus synced successfully." It clears itself after a few seconds. A blue box stays below it (see Undoing a sync).
  3. Open the syllabus page and refresh it. The template's current wording should be there, with the course's title, term, dates, credits, description, outcomes, textbook, banner image, and Week 1 materials in place.

Check each of those spots. A missing value or anything that looks off will show up here (see Editing course information).

docs.title: Undoing a sync
docs.text:
Sync saves to Canvas right away, and Canvas doesn't keep a version history for syllabi. To make a bad result recoverable, Sync keeps a copy of the previous syllabus in the browser that ran the sync.

After a sync:

  1. A box above the Sync button says when Sync ran and offers View syllabus (opens in a new tab), Undo sync, and Dismiss.
  2. The syllabus page shows a similar box at the top, with Undo sync and Looks good. Look the syllabus over. If something is wrong, click Undo sync and the syllabus returns to how it was before the sync. If it looks right, click Looks good to clear the box.

Things to know:

  • Only the most recent sync is kept. Syncing another course replaces the copy.
  • The copy is kept in the browser that ran the sync. It isn't available from another computer or browser profile, and clearing the browser's site data deletes it.
  • It is deleted automatically after 7 days, or as soon as Looks good or Dismiss is clicked.
  • If the syllabus was edited after the sync, Undo says so and asks before continuing, because undoing discards those edits.
  • If the message says undo isn't available, the browser couldn't save the copy.

docs.title: Editing course information
docs.text:
The course information table holds the details that are different for every course. Students see these values filled in as part of the syllabus (title and term in the top box, the description and outcomes under their headings, the textbook list under Textbook). The table itself is hidden from students.

To change one of these details, edit the table, not the syllabus text. The words on the syllabus page are filled in from the table when the page loads, so anything typed over them in the page is lost the next time the page loads or the syllabus is synced.

docs.title: Finding the table
docs.text:
Open the syllabus, click Edit, and look at the top of the page. The table has two columns: a name on the left and the course's value on the right.

Left column (don't change) What goes in the right column course-title Course number and title, e.g. BIOL 201: Ecology course-term The term code, e.g. DE5W11.16.26 course-dates The class dates, e.g. November 16 - December 20 credits A number, e.g. 3 course-description The course description, as plain text course-outcomes The outcomes, separated by \| (see below) textbook The textbook and required materials (see below)

Do not rename the names in the left column, add rows, or delete rows. The syllabus finds each value by that name.

Term and dates are also updated by the Update Start Date tool, so they rarely need to be typed by hand.

docs.title: The quirks
docs.text:
Lists use the pipe character |. A table cell can't hold a bulleted list, so lists are typed on one line with | between the items. The syllabus turns them into a real list when it displays.

  • Outcomes become a numbered list. Define key terms | Analyze a data set | Design an experiment displays as items 1, 2, and 3. Don't type the numbers.
  • Textbook becomes a bulleted list when there is more than one item. A single item is shown as plain text, not a list.
  • A | can't be used inside an item, because it is read as a break between items. Use a dash or a comma instead.
  • Spaces around the | don't matter.

Sub-bullets use || and |||. More pipes mean a deeper level. The number of pipes is how far in the item sits: | is a top-level item, || is indented one level, ||| is indented two.

Lab kit: order form | Required supplies || Gloves || Goggles | Textbook

displays as:

  • Lab kit: order form
  • Required supplies
  • Gloves
  • Goggles
  • Textbook

An item can only be one level deeper than the item before it. Nesting is for the textbook only; outcomes are always one flat numbered list.

Links work in the textbook, and only there. Add links in the textbook cell as usual (with the link button in the editor). Bold and italics are kept too. Links must start with http://, https://, or mailto:. In the description and outcomes, links and formatting are removed and only the text is shown.

Keep it simple. The cells show plain text (plus links, bold, and italics in the textbook). Colors, font sizes, images, and other formatting aren't carried over, so there is no point in adding them.

An empty cell shows nothing. If a value is missing, its spot on the syllabus is blank rather than showing an error. If part of the syllabus looks empty, check that its row in the table has a value.

Hidden from students, visible to editors. The table doesn't appear when the syllabus is displayed, but it is visible in the editor.

docs.title: If an error message appears
docs.text:
A failed sync shows a red Syllabus sync failed box at the top of the window, above the Show All Tests button. It says what went wrong and that the syllabus was not changed. Sync never writes a partial result, and no undo backup is kept for a failed sync.

The box has two buttons: Copy details copies the course name and id, the time, and the error text, which is what to send to Learning Technology if the problem can't be fixed from the table below. Dismiss closes the box.

Message What it means What to do This course's syllabus is missing its course meta table (table[data-course-meta]) and/or "Week 1 Learning Materials Preview" box. Nothing was changed. The syllabus doesn't have the course information table, the Week 1 Learning Materials Preview box, or both (the message lists which). Sync needs both to know what belongs to the course. Open the syllabus in edit mode. Check that the course information table is at the top and that the box titled Week 1 Learning Materials Preview is there and spelled that way. If either is missing, add it (or ask Learning Technology to migrate the syllabus), then try again. Couldn't find this course's syllabus. The course's syllabus is empty or couldn't be loaded. Open the syllabus page and make sure it has content. If it's empty, paste a saved copy back in (or copy one from a similar course), then try again. If it has content, refresh and try again. Couldn't find the template syllabus (template course ...). The template course for this type of course has no syllabus (or it couldn't be read). The number is the template course's id. Nothing is wrong with the course. Send the message to Learning Technology so the template can be checked. No template course found. The tool couldn't tell whether this is an undergraduate, graduate, or Career Edge course, so it doesn't know which template to use. Check the course code in the course's name or settings. If it looks right, tell Learning Technology. Error changing syllabus in course: ... followed by other text Canvas refused or failed the save, often a permissions or network problem. Refresh the page and try once more. If it fails again, use Copy details and send it to Learning Technology. The syllabus should be unchanged, but check it before moving on. Any other text in the red box An unexpected problem while loading the course, the template, or the syllabus. Refresh and try once more. If it fails again, use Copy details and send it to Learning Technology.

docs.title: After a sync, something looks wrong
docs.text:
• A value is missing or wrong (title, dates, outcomes, textbook). Edit it in the course information table as described above. The table is the single source for those values.
  • The Instructor Name link goes to the wrong course. Open the syllabus in edit mode and set the link on that line to the course's home page.
  • Something that was in the syllabus is gone. Only the four kept parts survive a sync. Use Undo sync (see above) to restore the previous syllabus, or add the content back.
  • A list looks flat when sub-bullets were expected, or | characters show on the page. The theme may not have loaded yet(though it's pretty dependable); refresh once. If || still shows as plain text, tell Learning Technology.

docs.title: ueu-canvas
docs.text:
This is the source code for the @ueu/ueu-canvas npm package — a TypeScript library for interacting with the Canvas LMS API. It provides typed interfaces, data fetching utilities, and helpers for working with Canvas objects such as courses, enrollments, content items, terms, users, rubrics, and files.

The package is built with Webpack and TypeScript and publishes its compiled output from the dist/ directory.

docs.title: What's in here

  • Enrollments — enrollment generators and role helpers
  • Terms — term fetching and date parsing from term names
  • Users — user generators
  • Fetch — low-level utilities for paginated Canvas API requests (getPagedDataGenerator, fetchJson, typed GET/write configs)
  • Rubrics — rubric and rubric association types and helpers
  • Files — Canvas file types
  • Mocks — mock data for testing

docs.title: LISA — Instructor Compliance Dashboard
docs.text: LISA is an "Instructor Insights"-style dashboard that allows deans to identify which instructors are behind on grading at a glance.

docs.title: Backend (lisa_backend)
docs.text:
Written in Python using Flask. Serves a REST API backed by a PostgreSQL database running in Docker.

Database & Canvas data

The database is created and maintained using the instructure-dap-client Python package, which pulls data from Canvas's Data Access Platform (DAP) into PostgreSQL. See this repo for the Docker configuration.

Note: The Canvas DAP client requires linux-based Python. The backend must run inside WSL, a VM, or natively on Linux. Python 3.11+ is required; Python 3.12 is currently used.

Key files

  • services/compliance_service.py — query logic
  • api_server.py — Flask routes and server startup
  • SQLAlchemy reflects Canvas-managed tables automatically; app-owned tables are defined as explicit models in models/models.py and managed by Alembic.

Authentication

The ldap3 package handles authentication against Unity's Microsoft Active Directory. Only members of a specific AD group can log in using their campus credentials. Users must be on the Unity intranet to access LISA.

WSGI

Waitress is used as the production WSGI server (port 5000).

docs.title: Frontend (lisa_frontend)
docs.text:
Written in TypeScript using React and Vite. Standard React/Vite app — see lisa_frontend/ for source.

In production, the frontend is built (npm run build) and the resulting dist/ folder is served by Flask/Waitress alongside the API.

docs.title: Production Server (unitycanvas-tcc)
docs.text:
Remote access to this machine is controlled by IT.

Web server — IIS

Microsoft IIS acts as a reverse proxy, handling inbound traffic and forwarding it to Waitress: - Application Request Routing (ARR) and URL Rewrite modules are installed to enable reverse proxy. - Reverse proxy is enabled in ARR settings. - URL Rewrite rules redirect HTTP to HTTPS and forward all traffic to the Waitress process on port 5000. - Bindings: HTTP on port 80, HTTPS on port 443. - SSL certificates were provisioned by IT. - Subdomains https://lisa and https://lisa.campus.unity.edu provided by IT

WSL

The backend runs inside WSL due to the Linux Python dependency. Ubuntu 22.04 is currently used.

To install pg_isready (used by the sync script): 

apt install postgresql

Scheduled sync

A cron job syncs the database twice daily via lisa_backend/scripts/run_sync.sh. Run lisa_backend/scripts/setup_sync_cron.sh to register it.

Database backups

lisa_backend/scripts/backup_db.sh dumps the database via the Docker container to /mnt/e/lisa_backups/ and prunes files older than 30 days. Run lisa_backend/scripts/setup_backup_cron.sh to register a daily midnight cron job for it.

Startup automation

Windows Task Scheduler is configured to automatically start Docker and run lisa_backend/scripts/launch_prod.sh inside WSL on machine startup.

docs.title: LISA Backend
docs.text: Flask API server for the LISA Instructor Compliance Dashboard. Pulls Canvas LMS data via the Instructure DAP client, stores it in PostgreSQL, and serves compliance metrics to the frontend.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 (required by scripts; 3.11+ is the minimum per DAP client docs)
  • Linux environment — the instructure-dap-client package requires linux-based Python. On Windows, run inside WSL.
  • PostgreSQL running and accessible (see Docker setup repo linked in the root README)
  • Node.js / npm — only needed if running the full dev stack via launch_dev.sh

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Create and populate .env

Copy env.example to .env and fill in all values. See Environment Variables below.

2. Install dependencies

uv sync

3. Initialize the database

The PostgreSQL database must already exist and be running. To populate it with Canvas data for the first time:

source .venv/bin/activate
python3.12 operate_db.py init all

This pulls all tracked tables from Canvas DAP into the database. It may take a while on first run.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
From the repo root, scripts/launch_dev.sh starts both the Flask backend (port 5001) and the Vite frontend dev server in one step:

bash lisa_backend/scripts/launch_dev.sh

The frontend dev server proxies /api requests to the Flask process, keeping session cookies on the same origin. Note: the backend does not auto-reload on file changes (use_reloader=False) — restart it manually after edits.

To run just the backend:

export FLASK_ENV=development
uv run python3.12 api_server.py

docs.title: Production
docs.text:
scripts/launch_prod.sh starts the Waitress WSGI server on port 5000 and automatically restarts it on non-zero exits:

bash lisa_backend/scripts/launch_prod.sh

In production, Flask also serves the compiled frontend from ../lisa_frontend/dist/. Build the frontend before starting the server:

cd ../lisa_frontend && npm run build

On unitycanvas-tcc, this script is launched automatically at startup via Windows Task Scheduler.

docs.title: Database Sync
docs.text:
Canvas data is kept current by syncing with the DAP API. The sync script waits for PostgreSQL to be ready before running:

bash lisa_backend/scripts/run_sync.sh

This calls python3.12 operate_db.py sync all under the hood. On the production server, a cron job runs this script twice daily.

You can also trigger a sync at any time from the UI, or invoke operate_db.py directly:

# Sync all tables
python3.12 operate_db.py sync all

# Sync specific tables
python3.12 operate_db.py sync submissions,assignments

# Initialize (first-time load) specific tables
python3.12 operate_db.py init enrollments,courses

Tracked tables: users, courses, enrollment_terms, assignments, submissions, enrollments, content_tags, context_modules, discussion_entries, discussion_topics, discussion_entry_participants, master_courses_child_subscriptions, submission_comments

submission_comments was added for the Rubric Compliance view. An existing database needs a one-time python3.12 operate_db.py init submission_comments followed by an API restart (the table is looked up when it is first needed, so the other endpoints keep working until then). Run the init when deploying this change: until then the nightly sync all reports a failure for submission_comments and exits non-zero, although the other tables still sync.

docs.title: Database Indexes
docs.text:
The following partial indexes exist on the canvas schema to support compliance queries. They are partial (i.e. indexed over a filtered subset of rows) because every query that joins on these tables always includes the filter condition — inactive/deleted rows are never needed. Partial indexes are smaller and faster than full indexes on the same columns since PostgreSQL only indexes the rows that queries actually touch.

submissions - idx_submissions_course_user_active — btree on (course_id, user_id) where workflow_state NOT IN ('unsubmitted', 'deleted')

enrollments - idx_enrollments_course_user_active — btree on (course_id, user_id) where workflow_state = 'active' - idx_enrollments_teacher_active — btree on (user_id, course_id) where workflow_state = 'active' AND type = 'TeacherEnrollment'

courses - idx_courses_term_id — btree on (enrollment_term_id)

docs.title: Suggested indexes
docs.text:
These would support the rubric compliance queries but are not created automatically; create them manually if the rubric endpoints are slow.

rubric_assessments - idx_rubric_assessments_submission_grading — btree on (artifact_id) where artifact_type = 'Submission' AND assessment_type = 'grading'

submission_comments - idx_submission_comments_submission — btree on (submission_id)

rubric_associations - idx_rubric_associations_assignment_active — btree on (association_id) where association_type = 'Assignment' AND workflow_state = 'active'

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Copy env.example to .env. All variables below are required for production.

Variable Description DAP_CLIENT_ID Instructure DAP API client ID DAP_CLIENT_SECRET Instructure DAP API client secret DAP_API_URL Instructure DAP API endpoint URL LISA_CANVAS_DB_NAME PostgreSQL database name LISA_CANVAS_DB_USER PostgreSQL username LISA_CANVAS_DB_PASSWORD PostgreSQL password LISA_CANVAS_DB_HOST PostgreSQL host (typically localhost) LISA_CANVAS_DB_PORT PostgreSQL port FLASK_ENV development or production FLASK_SECRET_KEY Secret key for Flask session encryption LDAP_SERVER LDAP server URL (e.g. ldaps://subdomain.domain.com) LDAP_BASE_DN Base DN for LDAP user searches LDAP_REQUIRED_GROUP Full CN of the AD group required for access IS_CE true for the CE deployment (optional, default false) CANVAS_BASE_URL Canvas instance the data comes from (optional) DEFAULT_TERM_ID Term used when a request names no term_id, and by /api/current_term when no term is running, e.g. between terms (optional; unset means term_id is required) OVERDUE_HOURS_DEFAULT / OVERDUE_HOURS_CE Hours before an ungraded submission is overdue (optional, default 72 / 48)

Security note: In production (FLASK_ENV=production), SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE is set to True, ensuring session cookies are only sent over HTTPS.

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text:
All endpoints are prefixed with /api. All except health and login require an active session: a dashboard (LDAP) session, except /api/search-* (Canvas session) and /api/terms (either).

Method Endpoint Description GET /api/health Server health and version info POST /api/login Authenticate with campus LDAP credentials POST /api/logout Clear session GET /api/me Current logged-in username GET /api/config Deployment settings for the dashboard (is_CE default, canvas_courses_url for links, default excluded_assignment_titles) GET /api/terms All terms, newest first, with start_at/end_at as YYYY-MM-DD Eastern dates GET /api/current_term Current UG/grad term (?isUnderGrad=true/false), else DEFAULT_TERM_ID's term; 404 if neither GET /api/dashboard/instructors Paginated grading compliance data per instructor GET /api/dashboard/discussion-instructors Paginated discussion response compliance data per instructor GET /api/dashboard/announcement-instructors Paginated announcement compliance data per instructor GET /api/dashboard/rubric-instructors Paginated rubric compliance data per instructor GET /api/grade-distribution Paginated per-assignment grade distribution stats for a term GET /api/instructor_conversations Paginated conversation stats per instructor (term_id, start_date, end_date, instructor_name; with a term_id, only that term's teachers and dates within it) GET /api/CALM_completion Paginated CALM module progress per student GET /api/CE-badge-grading Paginated CE badge grading per instructor and course in a term GET /api/search-* Paginated phrase search over syllabi, assignments, pages, topics, topic-replies, filenames, quizzes and questions GET /api/courses/<id>/submissions Submissions for a specific course GET /api/courses/<id>/rubric-submissions Graded rubric submissions for a specific course, with per-submission rubric line and comment counts GET /api/discussions/<id>/responses Discussion responses for a specific discussion POST /api/sync_request Trigger a Canvas DAP sync (async, returns 202) GET /api/last_sync Timestamp of last successful sync GET /api/violations List all flags, optionally filtered by flag_term_id, flag_type, instructor_id POST /api/violations Create a new flag (instructor_id, flag_type, flag_term_id required; reason_for_flag optional) GET /api/violations/<id> Get a single flag by ID PUT /api/violations/<id> Update flag type and/or reason DELETE /api/violations/<id> Delete a flag GET /api/violations/counts Per-instructor flag counts for a given term (flag_term_id required)

Every query param is optional except where marked required; leave a param out to get the endpoint's default. The shared parsing lives in utils/api_helpers.py:

  • Paging and sorting (every paginated endpoint): page, page_size (capped at MAX_PAGE_SIZE), sort_column, sort_direction. Any column in the result can be sorted on except JSON/array ones; an unknown sort_column or sort_direction falls back to the default. Paginated responses echo the sort that was applied as pagination.sort_column and pagination.sort_direction (used for the sort arrows), and the page_size that was used.
  • Term: term_id, defaulting to DEFAULT_TERM_ID (a 400 if neither is set). The frontend always sends the term it got from /api/current_term. The dashboard endpoints echo it as pagination.term_id. Conversations is the exception: with no term_id it covers every teacher.
  • Dates: start_date, end_date as YYYY-MM-DD, read as Eastern day bounds. A malformed date or a start after the end is a 400 with an error message. The grading, discussion and rubric instructor endpoints also reject dates outside the selected term, and so does conversations when a term_id is given.
  • Title filter: repeatable title_filter plus title_filter_mode (blacklist (default) or whitelist).

Instructor/discussion/announcement endpoint query params: paging and sorting, term_id, name, start_date, end_date, is_CE (defaults to the deployment's IS_CE). Instructors also take the title filter and overdue_hours (defaults to OVERDUE_HOURS_DEFAULT/OVERDUE_HOURS_CE); discussions take include_gallery.

Rubric instructor endpoint query params: paging and sorting (default graded_lines_pct ascending), term_id, name, start_date, end_date, is_CE and the title filter. The same params as the instructors endpoint minus overdue_hours. Each row has instructor_id, instructor_name, courses_this_term, the term totals rubric_submissions_term, rubric_unused_term, total_lines_term, graded_lines_term, graded_lines_pct (null when there are no lines), line_comments_pct (percent of total_lines_term, null when there are no lines), rubric_unused_pct and no_feedback_pct (percent of rubric_submissions_term, null when there are none), line_comments_term, submission_comments_term, no_feedback_term, and courses: one object per course with its course_id and rubric_submissions, rubric_unused, total_lines, graded_lines, line_comments, submission_comments and no_feedback, ordered by graded_lines ascending (all zero when the course has no rubric submissions).

Rubric submissions endpoint query params: paging and sorting (default graded_lines ascending, then submission_id), start_date, end_date, is_CE and the title filter. The dashboard sends the same values it used for the rubric instructor counts. Each row has submission_id, course_id, assignment_id, title, student_id, student_name, graded_at, cached_due_date, rubric_used, total_lines, graded_lines, line_comments and submission_comments.

Grade distribution endpoint query params: paging and sorting, term_id, course_code, title_filter (a single substring), group_by_section

Submissions endpoint query params: paging and sorting, start_date, end_date, is_CE and the title filter. The dashboard sends the same values it used for the grading counts.

Search endpoint query params: phrase (required), paging and sorting, course_name, term_id (no default: all terms), repeatable course_ids. Every result has course_id, course_name, term_id, id, title, workflow_state, created_at, updated_at and resource_link, plus type-specific columns. HTML tags are stripped before matching, so formatting doesn't split a phrase, and %/_ in the phrase match literally.

Violations list query params: flag_term_id, flag_type, instructor_id

docs.title: Compliance Logic
docs.text:
The core metric calculation lives in services/compliance_service.py. The key concept:

  • A submission is overdue if it has been sitting ungraded past the compliance window.
  • The window is 72 hours for standard courses and 48 hours for CE courses by default (OVERDUE_HOURS_DEFAULT/OVERDUE_HOURS_CE, or overdue_hours per request).
  • The window starts from the due date for on-time student submissions, or from the submission timestamp for late student submissions.

These thresholds are applied in get_compliance_for_courses(), which returns per-course counts that api_server.py aggregates per instructor.

Values that change per deployment (Canvas base URL, CE mode (IS_CE env var), search access role, DAP namespace, term name patterns, course code regex patterns, overdue thresholds, default excluded assignment titles and the fallback term) live in utils/config.py. Pagination defaults and default sort columns/directions are in utils/constants.py. Nothing is shared with the frontend by file: values it needs come from /api/config.

docs.title: Rubric compliance
docs.text:
Rubric compliance checks whether instructors fill out rubric lines and leave comments when grading. Like grading, it is course-level: every active teacher on a course is credited with that course's totals.

  • A submission counts if it passes the same filters as the grading view (dates on cached_due_date, CE mode, title filter, active student enrollment), its workflow_state is graded, and its assignment has an active grading rubric (a rubric_associations row with association_type = 'Assignment', purpose = 'grading', workflow_state = 'active') or the submission has a grading rubric assessment. A student with more than one active enrollment in the course (e.g. two sections) is counted once per submission.
  • The submission's rubric assessment is its most recently updated rubric_assessments row with artifact_type = 'Submission' and assessment_type = 'grading' (peer review and invited assessments are ignored). Its rubric is the assessment's rubric, or the assignment's rubric when there is no assessment.
  • rubric_used — a rubric assessment exists. Grading without opening the rubric leaves no assessment. Per course, rubric_submissions counts the submissions in scope and rubric_unused those without an assessment.
  • total_lines — the number of criteria in the rubric's data. If the rubric's data can't be read, the number of entries in the assessment instead (0 with no assessment).
  • graded_lines — assessment entries whose points is not null, capped at total_lines (so a rubric edited after grading can't push it past the total). 0 with no assessment. A rating named "blank" is still a chosen rating.
  • line_comments — assessment entries with a non-blank comments.
  • submission_comments — submission_comments rows on the submission that aren't drafts or peer review comments (assessment_request_id is null) and whose author has an active TeacherEnrollment in the course (TAs don't count).
  • no_feedback — a submission with no line comments and no submission comments.

The rubric and assessment data columns are JSON stored as text. They are parsed in Python rather than SQL (so the queries also run on the SQLite tests), and malformed or missing JSON counts as no entries. get_rubric_submissions() builds the per-submission query, get_rubric_criteria_counts() counts the criteria of the courses' rubrics, get_rubric_submission_stats() returns the per-submission counts for the drill-down, and get_rubric_compliance_for_courses() streams the same rows into per-course totals that api_server.py aggregates per instructor.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
uv run pytest

Tests live in tests/ and use an in-memory SQLite database — no credentials or running PostgreSQL required. regexp_replace and concat are registered on the SQLite connection so the search queries can run.

What's covered:

  • get_term_info — correct id→name mapping, empty table
  • get_current_term — UG vs grad selection (DE5W/DE8W), excludes "test" terms, excludes expired terms, overlapping terms
  • get_term — correct lookup, nonexistent term
  • get_submissions_to_courses — workflow state filtering (unsubmitted/deleted excluded), excluded assignment titles (Introductions, Integrity 1 & 2), CE vs non-CE due date requirement, start/end date filtering, inactive enrollment exclusion, course ID scoping
  • get_compliance_for_courses — on-time overdue, late overdue, graded not counted as overdue, within-window not counted, 48h vs 72h threshold, multi-course grouping, CE mode column differences, date range propagation
  • _rubric_line_stats — all/partial/null points, whitespace-only comments, bad or missing assessment JSON, unreadable rubric falling back to the assessment's entry count, graded lines capped at the total
  • get_rubric_submission_stats — fully assessed submission with comments, graded without the rubric (rubric_used false, total from the rubric), ungraded submissions and assignments without a rubric excluded, peer review assessments ignored, latest of two grading assessments wins, student/draft/peer review comments not counted, a teacher with two enrollments counted once, a teacher of another course not counted, inactive associations excluded, an assessment without an association still counted, unreadable rubric data falling back, a student in two sections counted once
  • get_rubric_criteria_counts — criteria counted per rubric, limited to the given courses' rubrics
  • get_rubric_compliance_for_courses — per-course aggregation, courses without rubric submissions absent
  • craft_instructors_courses_query — query construction (execution requires PostgreSQL due to array_agg and regex ~ operator)
  • search_* — phrases split by HTML, literal %/_, case and whitespace, course/term filters, the standard result columns
  • utils/api_helpers — page/sort parsing and clamping, date validation (incl. term bounds), title filter, paginate_query/paginate_list ordering and paging, cached, json_errors
